explanation: The scene gave English the phrase 'tilting at windmills', meaning fighting imaginary enemies. His squire, Sancho Panza, warns him beforehand that they are only windmills.

claims.text: In Don Quixote, the knight charges at windmills with his lance, believing them to be giants.
In this episode Don Quixote attacks windmills, not haystacks, oak trees or church towers.
The English phrase 'tilting at windmills', meaning fighting imaginary enemies, comes from this episode.
Sancho Panza warns Don Quixote that the giants are only windmills.
